reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of conformal prediction lies in transforming predictive models into valid uncertainty quantifiers through the use of conformity scores derived from residuals. In small-sample settings, standard quantile regression fails because it does not account for finite-sample variability. Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR) addresses this by computing prediction intervals based on the empirical distribution of conformity scores, which ensures finite-sample coverage under exchangeability. The Jackknife+ method improves upon CQR by avoiding data splitting, instead using leave-one-out residuals to construct intervals with a guaranteed minimum coverage of 1 - 2α. Split conformal further refines this by explicitly splitting data and estimating quantiles from the calibration set, offering distribution-free coverage guarantees. These methods collectively provide a hierarchy of approaches tailored to varying data scarcity levels, each maintaining rigorous statistical guarantees.
